article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Battle Against Malaria: A Goal Within Reach
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a threat in Kyamuyimbwa, Uganda (pop ~22,000), where Imelda’s story underscores the toll on mothers; preventive treatment and bed nets helped protect her next pregnancy. Since 2000, global malaria programs have averted about 2.3 billion cases and 14 million deaths, with 48 countries/territories eliminating malaria and three new eliminations in 2025. In the Greater Mekong subregion, cases fell nearly 90% despite drug resistance. Endemic countries declined from 108 in 2000 to ~80 in 2024; those reporting under 10,000 cases rose from 27 to 46. Progress is driven by vaccines, better medicines, vector control, and innovations like gene-modified mosquitoes and long-acting injectables, enabling proactive, sustainable control. Yet 2024 recorded 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths; challenges include artemisinin and pyrethroid resistance, urban Anopheles stephensi, and diagnostic mutations. Global malaria funding in 2024 was $3.9B vs $9.3B needed for 2025, a $5.4B gap. World Malaria Day 2026 theme calls for resolve; examples include Mauritius and China; Vietnam reports 2025: 246 cases, early 2026: 25, near elimination by 2030.

article.articleHeadline: 'Vaca louca' e a doação de sangue no Brasil - 24/04/2026 - Tv Folha - Folha
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 'Mad cow disease' and blood donation in Brazil - April 24, 2026 - Tv Folha - Folha
article.articleSummary: Brazil restricts blood donation for people who lived in Europe due to concerns about Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE, mad cow disease) and the risk of transmitting the human form, variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (vCJD). BSE affects cattle and is caused by prions that damage neurons; vCJD is fatal in humans. Europe’s BSE outbreak began in the United Kingdom in 1986; the 1993 peak exceeded 100,000 cattle cases, with spread to other European countries. Worldwide, 233 people have contracted vCJD, with the last case recorded about a decade ago. There is no blood test to detect prions, underpinning precautionary measures in Brazil: donors who spent more than five years in Europe after 1980, or more than three months in the United Kingdom or Ireland between 1980-1996, are barred. Brazil has never reported a human vCJD case and the Health Ministry is reviewing these rules against international practices.

article.articleSummary: World Malaria Day on April 25 highlights malaria awareness. Junagadh district in Gujarat remains malaria-free, recording only one case in the four months of 2026. Historical data show 2023–24 had 23 malaria cases (16 men, 7 women) and 2025 had 25 cases (13 men, 12 women). As of 2026 so far, just one male case has been reported. Civil Surgeon advises prompt medical attention if chills followed by high fever, headache, dizziness or vomiting occur. Malaria is transmitted by mosquitoes; thus maintaining cleanliness in homes and streets and preventing standing water is essential to curb mosquito breeding. The article notes malaria types but does not provide details.

article.articleHeadline: Em pacote de R$ 27,5 milhões para saúde e combate a chikungunya, unidade móvel é inaugurada em reserva indígena de Dourados
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: As part of a R$ 27.5 million package for health and the fight against chikungunya, a mobile unit is inaugurated in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve.
article.articleSummary: On 25 April 2026, Brazil’s Health Ministry opened a mobile health unit at Bororó II in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, 226 km from Campo Grande, as part of a R$27.5 million package to strengthen health services and fight chikungunya. The ceremony featured Indigenous Health Secretariat head Lucinha Tremembé and Family Health Department director José Eudes Barroso, underscoring near-access care for Indigenous communities. The package earmarks R$19.3 million per year to expand MAC (Medium and High Complexity) services at Hospital Regional de Dourados (HRD) and R$325,000 annually to Hospital Universitário de Dourados (HU). It also funds 20 ICU beds (10 adults and 10 pediatrics) at HRD, with an annual impact of R$3.94 million, boosting capacity to manage severe chikungunya cases amid rising demand. The plan reinforces federal efforts to improve qualified, local care for Indigenous populations.

article.articleHeadline: Bangladesh remains at high risks from measles
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak in Bangladesh remains high risk; WHO assesses national risk as high due to ongoing transmission, a large susceptible pool, immunity gaps, and deaths. From March 15 to early April 2026, 4,231 confirmed and 29,549 suspected measles cases have been reported across 58 of 64 districts, with 42 confirmed and 198 suspected deaths. Dhaka, Rajshahi, Chattogram, and Khulna bear the heaviest burden; Dhaka records 8,263 suspected cases, including clusters in Demra, Jatrabari, Kamrangirchar, Korail, Mirpur, and Tejgaon. Children under five account for 79% of cases (under two: 66%; under nine months: 33%). The outbreak follows suboptimal immunity after MR1/MR2 vaccine stockouts in 2024–2025 and no nationwide campaigns since 2020; some infections occur before 9 months. Cross-border risk with India and Myanmar is noted. WHO recommends strengthened surveillance, rapid response, continued vaccination stock, and campaigns; no travel restrictions.

article.articleSummary: World Malaria Day 2026 (April 25) from the Lifestyle Desk in New Delhi promotes six home remedies to transform homes into a no-mosquito zone and shield residents from malaria, dengue, and chikungunya. With India facing malaria and vectored illnesses, the piece emphasizes preventive measures during the hot season and aligns the message with World Malaria Day’s public health outreach. article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day: Asymptomatic Patients' Real Challenge To Make MP Malaria-Free
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Madhya Pradesh, India, faces a hidden burden as asymptomatic infections resist standard microscopy and rapid diagnostic tests. On World Malaria Day, April 25, 2026, authorities report that 27% of febrile patients carry malaria undetected by routine tests, complicating elimination efforts. National Health Mission data identify about 700 asymptomatic cases in Balaghat, and 100 cases each in Chhindwara, Narsinghpur, and Jhabua districts. These silent infections—parasites at low levels—enable ongoing transmission, especially among tribal populations identified as highly vulnerable. Health officials warn that asymptomatic carriers are a major challenge to achieving Madhya Pradesh’s goal of malaria elimination by 2030. The findings underscore the need for more sensitive surveillance and targeted interventions to detect and treat hidden infections beyond conventional microscopy and RDTs.

article.articleHeadline: Đổ xô lên tuyến trên khám tay chân miệng, tăng nguy cơ phát tán dịch bệnh
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rush to top-tier hospitals for hand-foot-mouth disease examinations, increasing the risk of spreading the disease.
article.articleSummary: HFMD is peaking in Ho Chi Minh City, with 58 inpatients in the Infectious-Neurology ward at Children's Hospital 1, up about 20% from last week. About one-third of admissions are severe and require emergency care. The outbreak is expected to continue February–June, with most severe cases linked to Enterovirus 71 (EV71); other strains are milder. About 65% of hospitalized children come from neighboring provinces. There is no evidence that dietary supplements prevent HFMD; strict hygiene remains the defense until a vaccine is available. Parents should seek care at local facilities to avoid long trips and wider spread. Early detection requires collaboration among health services, schools, and families; around 10% of adults may be asymptomatic carriers. Signs include vesicles on palms, soles, knees, buttocks, elbows, and mouth ulcers; home isolation about 7 days. Red flags: persistent high fever; startling sleep; vomiting, unsteady gait, tremors, or rapid breathing—urgent care.

triage.headline_ja: 手足口病の検査を求めて上級病院に殺到、疾病拡散のリスク増加

triage.notes: 記事は2026年4月配信（将来日付）となっているが、内容は2月～6月の季節性流行を示唆。EV71による重症例の存在、約65%が近隣州からの患者で広域移動が確認され、長期曝露と流行感受性が高い。ホーチミン市の小児病院で58名の入院患者が確認されている。

article.articleSummary: World Malaria Day, observed on 25 April 2026, promotes proactive prevention and control of malaria. Malaria is an infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites. Transmission from an infected person to a healthy person occurs primarily via vectors, mainly Anopheles mosquitoes. To prevent and control malaria, the article states that the first priority is implementing measures to avoid mosquito bites. The report, from Vietnam News Agency (TTXVN/Bao Tin Tuc and Dan Toc), does not include country-specific case counts or outbreaks. Instead, it emphasizes public health actions to reduce transmission and protect at-risk populations. The central message is that reducing exposure to mosquito bites is the essential frontline strategy in combating malaria, as highlighted in the World Malaria Day coverage dated 25 April 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Descubren en Kenia un nuevo coronavirus en murciélagos capaz de infectar células humanas - La Banda Diario
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New coronavirus in bats in Kenya capable of infecting human cells discovered - La Banda Diario
article.articleSummary: New coronavirus CcCoV-KY43 detected in bats in Kenya can invade human cells via the CEACAM6 receptor. Researchers screened 27 bat coronavirus spike proteins and found CcCoV-KY43 uses CEACAM6; overexpressing CEACAM6 rendered human cells susceptible. Serology of people near Kenyan bat roosts showed no recent infections by this virus. Related Kenyan bat coronaviruses also use CEACAM6; some bat coronaviruses from Russia and China could use similar receptors in other mammals. The work involved Pirbright Institute confirming cellular infection, York University identifying the receptor, Cambridge University solving the structure, the National Museums of Kenya detecting the virus in bats, and KEMRI-Wellcome Trust analyzing local sera. Recommendations: bolster bat coronavirus surveillance and monitor CEACAM6 as a potential entry pathway. Limitations: the study used synthetic proteins and lab models, not the live virus; real-world behavior remains unknown. The goal is predicting zoonotic risk from sequence alone.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアのコウモリで発見された新型コロナウイルス CcCoV-KY43 が人間の細胞に感染可能 - La Banda Diario

triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアでのバットコロナウイルス検出だが、対象国リストにケニアが含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。サマリーにはロシアと中国のコウモリコロナウイルスについても言及されており、中国は対象国のため含める。現時点では人間への実際の感染報告がなく（血清検査で近隣住民に最近の感染なし）、合成タンパク質と実験室モデルを用いた研究段階であることが重要。今後の実地監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Duy trì bền vững kết quả công tác phòng, chống sốt rét
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sustaining the results of malaria prevention and control efforts.
article.articleSummary: Malaria, caused by Plasmodium species (P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale, P. knowlesi) and transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes, remains a public health focus in Lao Cai Province, Vietnam. Local health centers implement ongoing prevention, surveillance, early detection, diagnosis, and treatment, plus community education on bed-net use, personal protection in forests, and environmental hygiene. The highland commune of Pha Long is prioritized due to accessibility challenges and population mobility, with efforts targeting workers and returnees from malaria-endemic areas or abroad. In late 2025, field sampling in Gia Phú under an Artemisinin-resistant malaria project strengthened drug-resistance monitoring. Cross-border collaboration with China–Vietnam partners on tropical diseases was also emphasized. Since 2011–2020, Lao Cai achieved indigenous malaria elimination in 2020; now the focus is on preventing reintroduction and sustaining nationwide elimination by 2030, supported by multi-sector cooperation and international projects.

article.articleHeadline: Why is India still struggling to end malaria?
article.articleSummary: Malaria in India remains a public health challenge. As of early 2026, India reported an 80.5% decline in cases and 78% in deaths from 2015–2023, with 83 deaths and about 1.765 million suspected/confirmed cases in 2023. India aims to eliminate malaria by 2030, but high-burden tribal areas—Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and northeastern states—remain. WHO has certified over 40 countries malaria-free, including Egypt (2024), China (2021), and Sri Lanka (2016). Experts cite surveillance gaps, inequity, and structural health-system issues, plus diverse epidemiology requiring district-tailored approaches. Mosquitoes are adapting: outdoor biting, dawn/dusk activity, and insecticide resistance reduce indoor spraying and nets. Asymptomatic reservoirs complicate elimination; recommendations include maintaining microscopy, scalable rapid diagnostics, molecular tests, and xenomonitoring. Vaccines are advancing: two licensed vaccines, including Serum Institute’s; R21/MM deployed; vivax vaccines and long-acting injectables in development.

triage.notes: 記事は2023年のデータに基づくインドのマラリア流行分析であり、2030年根絶目標に向けた現在進行形の課題を扱っている。オディシャ州とチャッティスガル州など高負担地域が特定されている。発生地域リストにはエジプト、スリランカ、中国が含まれているが、記事サマリーではこれらは比較対象（マラリア認定排除国）として言及されているに過ぎず、実際のイベント発生地ではないため、verified_locationsはインドのみとした。

article.articleHeadline: Prefeitura abre contratação de médicos e enfermeiros para enfrentar Chikungunya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: City Hall opens recruitment of doctors and nurses to combat Chikungunya.
article.articleSummary: Dourados Municipal Hall opened emergency recruitment for doctors and nurses to combat the Chikungunya epidemic amid a public health emergency. Edital No. 27/2026/SEMS/PMD calls for temporary contracts for physicians and nurses to work in Basic Health Units, Emergency Care Units, and public or contracted hospitals. The move follows decrees establishing a Center for Public Health Emergency Operations (COE) and a declared health calamity due to Chikungunya, with rising cases and risk of public-system collapse. Applications are to be submitted to the Municipal Health Secretariat in Dourados, Rua Coronel Ponciano, 900, 8:00–13:00, with documents including photo ID or professional ID, CPF, proof of education, professional registration, and proof of at least five years’ experience. Selection ranks by verified experience; ties broken by older age. The hires are temporary and limited to the emergency period.

article.articleHeadline: Puluhan Siswa Kediri Mual & Muntah, SPPG Ditutup Sementara, Ditemukan Bakteri E. coli di MBG
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dozens of Kediri students with nausea and vomiting; SPPG temporarily closed; Escherichia coli bacteria found at MBG.
article.articleSummary: On 22 April 2026, 69 students from SDN Ketami 1, SDN Ketami 2, and SDN Tempurejo 1 in Ketami, Kediri City, experienced nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and fever after participating in the Free Nutritious Meal Program (MBG/SPPG). The Kediri City MBG Task Force reported that Escherichia coli (E. coli) was detected in MBG meals, indicating the food was not fit for consumption. The program was temporarily closed as authorities investigate. Health authorities collected food samples for laboratory testing and conducted follow-up checks at MBG Tempurejo. No student required inpatient care; most have improved and Puskesmas continues monitoring. The city government, in coordination with the National Nutrition Agency (Badan Gizi Nasional), will review SOPs and monitoring to prevent recurrence while keeping MBG active under tightened oversight.

article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day 2026: Symptoms, Prevention, And Latest Treatments | News18
article.articleSummary: World Malaria Day 2026 highlights WHO’s campaign 'Driven to End Malaria: Now We Can. Now We Must' to eliminate malaria, a mosquito-borne disease causing 610,000 deaths annually. Since 2000, 2.3 billion cases and 14 million deaths have been averted. As of 2024, 47 countries have been certified malaria-free (including two in 2024 and three in 2025); endemic countries fell from 108 in 2000 to 80 today. In 2024 there were estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths. RTS,S/AS01 vaccine rolled out in 25 countries, protecting 10 million children; next-generation insecticide-treated nets account for 84% of new nets. Symptoms appear 7–30 days after bites: fever, chills, headaches, muscle/joint pain, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; severe cases cause jaundice, anemia, convulsions, coma. Early diagnosis and ACTs are standard; pregnant women require tailored regimens (often quinine with clindamycin in first trimester). India targets elimination by 2030; diagnostics to detect low-density infections are critical.

article.articleSummary: As of 25 April 2026, Pattaya, Thailand launches a rabies-control campaign offering free pet sterilization and rabies vaccination to curb stray dogs and cats amid rising stray populations linked to abandonment. The event, chaired by Mayor Poramet Ngampichet at Wat Nong Yai, marks the national Rabies-Free Animals, Safe Communities initiative inspired by Princess Chulabhorn Walailak. Pattaya’s veterinary team pursues mass vaccination, sterilization, and relocation of stray animals to the Pong subdistrict shelter, in cooperation with Pattaya Animal Hospital. Rabies remains fatal once symptoms appear, underscoring preventive vaccination and population management to protect public health and tourism image. Mobile units will operate through late April with Walking Street (April 27), Kophai (April 28), and Thappraya (April 29) visits. Services, including broader health screenings by Pattaya Bhattamakun Hospital, and access details via the Veterinary Division or 1337, are provided to Pattaya residents with registration and ID.

article.articleHeadline: Tập trung nguồn lực loại trừ sốt rét
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Concentrate resources to eradicate malaria
article.articleSummary: World Malaria Day 2026 theme: concentrate resources to eliminate malaria in Vietnam by 2030. Thanh Hoa Province, malaria-free since 2020, still faces risk due to population movement and returnees from endemic areas; over 6,200 people remain in high-risk groups. In March 2026, no malaria cases or deaths were reported; disease remains controlled but vigilance is essential. Surveillance requires testing all suspected cases and reporting within 48 hours; microscopy labs must be maintained to detect parasites. Treatment aims for 100% of patients to receive correct regimens to avoid relapse and drug resistance, with imported cases monitored. Vector control includes mosquito surveillance, targeted insecticide spraying, long-lasting insecticide-treated nets, and environmental hygiene campaigns. Public education via media and community outreach emphasizes protective behaviors for high-risk groups. Sustained vigilance is essential to meet the 2030 elimination goal and prevent reintroduction through population movement.

Diagnosis is confirmed via blood tests, after which doctors prescribe medications based on the patient’s condition. The piece warns against self-medicating based on symptoms, as improper use of drugs can pose additional risks. Risk reduction requires protection from mosquitoes and prompt medical consultation. Emphasis is placed on awareness, timely diagnosis, and expert medical guidance for effective treatment.

article.articleHeadline:
南财健康科普
                                流感季仍需警惕！疾控专家：三价疫苗完全能覆盖当前流行毒株
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The flu season still requires vigilance! Disease-control experts: the trivalent vaccine fully covers the currently circulating strains.
article.articleSummary: Influenza remains the leading respiratory pathogen in China in 2026, with Week 16 sentinel surveillance (Apr 13–19) showing influenza viruses causing 13.4% of ILI samples, ahead of rhinovirus (9.3%) and parainfluenza (6.7%); activity is declining but ongoing. China faces an annual burden of roughly 84–144 million influenza cases. WHO's 2025–2026 guidance states since 2020 no natural B/Yamagata lineage detected, so trivalent vaccines are sufficient to cover circulating strains. Domestic vaccine options include trivalent and quadrivalent formulations across platforms; by Nov 2025, 389 batches were issued. In procurement, trivalent vaccines price dropped to 5.5 yuan, while quadrivalent vaccines remain pricier in private markets. Beijing data show vaccine impact hinges on uptake: ≥50% coverage in schools dramatically reduces transmission; elderly uptake remains suboptimal despite free programs since 2007, with 471 clinics and expanded free vaccination for frontline workers since 2024. Immunization is a national legal priority; increasing adult vaccination is emphasized.

article.articleHeadline: O Aedes ainda resiste
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Aedes Still Resists
article.articleSummary: Rio Preto, in Northwest São Paulo, faced a severe dengue burden in 2025 with over 52,000 cases and 40 deaths. The article stresses that dengue control cannot be seasonal or limited to rainy periods; the Aedes aegypti mosquito continues circulating during dry spells, finding shelter in often overlooked containers and water storage inside homes. Vigilance must be year-round, as small lapses feed large outbreaks. Responsibility is collective: residents should remove breeding sites, keep water tanks sealed, clear gutters, and discard items that collect water. Yet citizen action alone is insufficient; sustained investments in health infrastructure, field workers, and monitoring are essential, alongside transparent data sharing and active community engagement. Ignoring dengue outside the rainy season risks repeating a costly cycle. Rio Preto’s recent memory should catalyze lasting prevention year-round rather than accepting high case counts.

article.articleHeadline: Paljonko suomalaisia tulee kuolemaan koronavirukseen?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How many Finns will die from the coronavirus?
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Finland could, as of 25 April 2026, result in 15,000–115,000 deaths and infect 1.65–3.85 million of Finland’s ~5.5 million people, potentially more than wartime losses. Global infection may reach 30–70% of the world’s population with a 1–3% fatality rate; mortality would be heaviest among the elderly and those with conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and heart or lung disease, where death rates could be 5–15%. The article notes Finland’s scenario could yield a lifetime risk of roughly 1 in 300, or perhaps 1 in 50, of Finns dying. Worldwide deaths could total 20–160 million; only China and South Korea have contained the outbreak to date. Without quarantines, infections might reach 0.4–1 billion and deaths 4–30 million. Three mitigation steps: rigorous handwashing for 20–30 seconds and avoiding face-touching; minimizing close contact, especially with risk groups; and preserving health-system capacity by using emergency services only when needed and consulting a helpline for suspected cases.

article.articleHeadline: Vết trầy xước - cửa ngõ bệnh 'sốt đất' xâm nhập cơ thể
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A scratch wound - the gateway for the disease 'soil fever' to invade the body.
article.articleSummary: Burkholderia pseudomallei causes melioidosis, or soil fever, contracted from contaminated soil or water and typically entering via skin wounds; person-to-person transmission is not reported. Initial symptoms are non-specific—fever, fatigue, myalgia, malaise—with skin wounds that may lack signs, delaying diagnosis. Untreated, bacteria can disseminate hematogenously, causing abscesses in the lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, bones or prostate, and septicemia with high mortality. Risk factors include diabetes, chronic liver or kidney disease, and alcohol use; high-risk occupations include farmers, environmental workers, and construction workers. Prevention emphasizes wound cleaning, hygiene, gloves and boots when handling soil or mud, and avoiding contact with contaminated water. In Thailand (as of 2026-04-25), melioidosis has 732 cases and 23 deaths. Early recognition and treatment are crucial to reduce mortality.

article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day 2026: From Dengue to Zika, 7 mosquito-borne diseases and prevention tips
article.articleSummary: World Malaria Day 2026 highlights ongoing malaria burden in tropical and subtropical regions, caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes, with seven major mosquito-borne diseases to watch: dengue, chikungunya, Zika, Japanese encephalitis, lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis), and yellow fever, transmitted by Anopheles, Aedes, and Culex species. Malaria presents with high fever, chills, sweating, headache, nausea, and fatigue; severe disease can affect the brain, kidneys, or lungs. Zika can cause fever, rash, conjunctivitis, and joint pains, with birth defects risk in pregnancy. Yellow fever causes fever, jaundice, and bleeding, notably in Africa and South America. Prevention emphasizes eliminating stagnant water, repellents, protective clothing, nets, and community fumigation and awareness. Early diagnosis is crucial; Indian doctors warn of shifting mosquito patterns due to urbanisation and climate change, urging vigilance during monsoon.

article.articleHeadline: Perubahan Iklim Perluas Ancaman Penyakit Menular, Anak Paling Rentan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Climate change expands the threat of infectious diseases, with children most vulnerable.
article.articleSummary: Climate change expands the threat of infectious diseases, with dengue fever spreading beyond tropical zones into subtropical and cooler regions, endangering children who are not fully immunized. IDAI Immunization Task Force head Hartono Gunardi told a Jakarta press conference on April 23 that warmer temperatures allow dengue-carrying mosquitoes to reach wider areas and increase incidence. In addition to dengue, measles poses renewed risk as the virus remains weather-resistant; in 2025–2026 Europe and the Americas reported outbreaks. In Europe alone, about 40 countries are affected by measles outbreaks. Measles symptoms include fever and red rash, potentially progressing to pneumonia and other complications, including hearing loss, corneal damage, and rarely encephalitis. Emphasizing routine immunization, Gunardi urged completing vaccines for children to prevent future outbreaks and support educational outcomes.

triage.headline_ja: 気候変動が感染症の脅威を拡大、子どもが最も脆弱

triage.notes: 記事はジャカルタでの公式声明（2026年4月23日、インドネシア小児科医学会予防接種対策部長による）に基づいており、デング熱の拡大、麻疹の国際的流行（ヨーロッパ約40カ国）、および気候変動による感染症リスク増加を報道。ただし、インドネシア内での具体的なアウトブレイク事例（患者数、死亡数、地域情報）の詳細が不足しており、ヨーロッパ・アメリカの麻疹流行の具体情報も対象国外であるため検証対象外。続報で具体的な患者数、発症地域、対応状況の情報待機。

article.articleSummary: Malaria affected Maharashtra heavily last year, with 23,247 cases and 27 deaths in the state; Mumbai reported 10,162 cases and 7 deaths, according to the Public Health Department. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, notably P. vivax and P. falciparum, with the latter being highly lethal. World Malaria Day on 25 April highlights prevention; authorities urge cleanliness, elimination of standing water, and mosquito protection, stressing citizen participation. The disease now appears year-round, not just during the monsoon, with fever that can recur and delays in treatment risking severe illness. Dr. Vinayak Sawardekar, Superintendent of St. George Hospital, emphasizes timely treatment as crucial. The article underscores ongoing public health challenges and the need for preventive measures to curb malaria transmission.

article.articleHeadline: कागजों में काबू, जमीन पर कहर; ओडिशा में मलेरिया उन्मूलन सबसे बड़ी चुनौती  - odisha malaria surge a challenge to indias eradication goal
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Under control on paper, havoc on the ground; malaria eradication in Odisha is the biggest challenge.
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Odisha remains India’s biggest challenge. Odisha accounted for about 26.7% of India's 2024 malaria burden (roughly 68,600 of 257,000 cases). In Odisha, 83% of cases originate from six districts—Kalahandi, Raigarh, Kandhamal, Koraput, Malkangiri, and Mayurbhanj—driven by rugged terrain, limited health access, and low awareness. Nationally, Jharkhand reported 42,352 and Chhattisgarh 33,023, highlighting Odisha as the principal hurdle to a broader control, according to authorities. Persistent bottlenecks include shortages of insecticide-treated nets, delays in distribution, and a slowing 'Daman' vector-control program. The government plans to re-energize Daman, launch hotspot screening camps, and roll out new nets, aiming to reduce local malaria cases to zero by 2027 and achieve elimination by 2030. World Malaria Day 2026 theme: 'Inspired to End Malaria: Now We Can, Now We Must.'

triage.notes: オディシャはインドのマラリア症例の約26.7%を占める主要な流行地域。複数州（オディシャ、ジャールカンド、チャッティスガル）での持続的な感染とベクター対策の不備がWPRO基準全項目で該当。政府は2027年までの地域症例ゼロ化と2030年の排除達成を目標としており、政策的な関心も高い。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kafka and Wolker were treated in the High Tatras. Tuberculosis is on the rise again in the Czech Republic.
article.articleSummary: In 2024, the Czech Republic logged 429 tuberculosis cases, including 134 Ukrainians, 16 Slovaks, 13 Vietnamese, 9 Romanians, and 8 Bulgarians. Foreigners comprised 225 cases, two-thirds of them from Ukraine. Since January, a Czech Ministry of Health regulation requires foreigners from high-prevalence countries who apply for work to be screened for TB, with pulmonologists calling for chest X-ray screening for all long-term residence applicants from risk countries. The risk countries include Ukraine, Romania, the Philippines, India, Georgia, China, and South Africa. Experts note persistent TB stigma, which can hinder diagnosis and treatment. These figures underscore ongoing cross-border transmission and the need for targeted screening and surveillance to curb imported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Telangana moves closer to malaria elimination goal
article.articleSummary: Telangana moved closer to its 2030 malaria elimination goal as World Malaria Day data show a steady decline in cases and continued low transmission. From 874 cases in 2021, annual malaria infections fell to 611 (2022), 420 (2023), 269 (2024), and 259 (2025). In 2025, 11 districts, including Jagtial, Suryapet, Medak and Kamareddy, reported zero cases, and the state is categorized as Category 1 by Annual Parasite Incidence, indicating a low malaria burden. The state has achieved over 98% reduction since 2014, when infections were around 14,000. The 3T strategy—Test, Treat and Track—has been central to progress. Officials credited strengthened surveillance, early diagnosis, timely treatment, and frontline workers like ASHA staff for case identification and containment. Vector control relies on administrative action and community participation, with improved sanitation and awareness aiding decline.

article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day 2026: क्यों होता है मलेरिया? डेंगू से कितना अलग
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Malaria Day 2026: Why does malaria occur? How is it different from dengue?
article.articleSummary: World Malaria Day 2026 highlights malaria transmission via infected Anopheles mosquitoes and the Plasmodium parasite, which targets blood and liver. Malaria remains a major health issue in India and other countries, with risk rising in areas where dirty water and standing water accumulate during warm seasons and monsoons. Malaria and dengue are both mosquito-borne, but differ: malaria is caused by a parasite, dengue by a virus. Malaria commonly presents with chills, high fever, sweating, and headache, while dengue features sudden high fever, eye or body pains, and may include red skin rashes and rapidly falling platelets. Prevention focuses on reducing mosquito exposure: eliminate standing water, sleep under nets, apply repellents, wear covered clothing, keep surroundings clean, and occasionally spray insecticides. Seek medical care promptly if fever appears, per Dr. Subhash Giri of RML Hospital.

article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day: Key symptoms and risks in children, when parents should seek urgent care
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a serious concern for children in regions with mosquito-borne illnesses, highlighted on World Malaria Day 2026 (April 25) in New Delhi. Dr Sunny Lohia, Consultant Paediatric, Apollo Spectra Hospital, warns that malaria in children can progress faster than in adults, making early recognition crucial. Key symptoms include repeated fever with chills and sweating, unusual sleepiness or low activity, poor feeding and vomiting, irritability or excessive crying, and in some cases breathing difficulty. Delays in diagnosis can lead to dehydration and anaemia and other severe complications. In malaria-prone areas, any fever should be tested promptly rather than treated at home. Early diagnosis and timely medical care improve recovery and prevent serious risks. Parents should monitor behaviour changes and seek urgent care if a child becomes unusually drowsy or experiences breathing trouble.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria beyond mosquito bites: How your daily habits and living conditions increase infection risk
article.articleSummary: Malaria risk in India extends beyond mosquito bites, with daily habits and living conditions shaping infection risk. As of October 2025, India reported over 2.02 lakh malaria cases (NCVBDC), with elimination targeted by 2027 and complete eradication by 2030. Environment matters: poor drainage, stagnant or open water sources, and contaminated surroundings create ideal mosquito habitats, while open water containers, blocked drains, or water in coolers raise exposure. Protection relies on nets, repellents, and window screens, especially at night when vectors are most active. Cerebral malaria, usually due to Plasmodium falciparum, can progress to seizures, confusion, loss of consciousness, coma, and death as infected blood cells block brain vessels. Early diagnosis is often missed because symptoms resemble other neurological conditions, impacting adults, children, and pregnant women. The article emphasizes daily-life practices as a key protective measure against malaria.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Malaria Day: The double attack of dengue-typhoid alongside malaria increases trouble, posing a challenge for doctors.
article.articleSummary: Co-infections of malaria with dengue, chikungunya, or typhoid are emerging in Delhi, India, complicating diagnosis and treatment. A study at Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital analyzed 4,259 fever patients from July 2022 to November 2023, identifying 87 malaria-positive cases (2.04%). Among these, about 45% had co-infection with dengue, chikungunya, or typhoid. Both Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum were detected. Predominant symptoms included chills (80.5%), jaundice (51.7%), muscle and body aches (56.3% and 54.0%), and hepatosplenomegaly (64.4%), with anemia as a major complication in severe cases. Diagnostic challenges arise when infections overlap, particularly during July–September; men showed higher risk than women. Transmission involves urban mosquito vectors, while typhoid relates to contaminated water and poor sanitation. Preventive measures include use of mosquito nets, eliminating standing water, wearing long-sleeved clothing, and seeking prompt medical care for fever.

article.articleHeadline: DOH warns people with HIV at higher risk of tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: DOH warns that people living with HIV in Manila, Philippines are at higher risk of tuberculosis due to HIV-induced immune suppression. HIV attacks CD4 T-cells, the immune system’s managers, and when these cells dwindle, the body’s defenses against bacteria weaken. This creates a window for opportunistic infections such as TB to emerge. TB bacteria can lie dormant inside the body, usually controlled by a strong immune system, but HIV weakens immunity so TB can wake up and become active disease. The advisory, issued via a Manila DOH post on 2026-04-25, underscores the need for heightened TB awareness and monitoring among PLHIV. No specific case counts, deaths, or outbreak details are provided in the article.

article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day: Doctor Explains The Difference Between Normal Fever And Malaria Fever
article.articleSummary: Malaria fever differs from ordinary fevers in the context of World Malaria Day 2026. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes, with cyclic fever episodes—sharp temperature spikes followed by chills, sweating, and a recurrence typically every 2-3 days, depending on parasite species. Associated symptoms include headaches, nausea/vomiting, and fatigue, with intermittent normal periods between fevers. Normal fever, usually due to viral or bacterial infections, tends to rise gradually and resolve with time and standard care. Environmental factors like stagnant water and monsoon season raise malaria risk in India, including regions such as Gurugram. If untreated, malaria can cause anemia, jaundice, and liver/kidney impairment. Diagnosis is via simple blood test; treatment requires malaria-specific medications and should not rely on paracetamol alone. Seek care if fever lasts >48–72 hours, per Dr. Shailesh Sahay (Max Hospital, Gurugram).

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pattaya steps up safety measures and animal welfare as part of a rabies campaign - Pattaya Mail
article.articleSummary: Rabies prevention drives Pattaya, Thailand to launch a citywide health program offering free pet sterilization and vaccination to curb a rising stray dog and cat population and reduce rabies risk. The campaign, titled Animals without Rabies, Safe Communities, formally opened on 24 April at Wat Nong Yai temple, led by Mayor Poramet Ngampichhet and under national sponsorship from Princess Chulabhorn Walailak. In addition to vaccination and sterilization, stray animals are directed to a municipal shelter in the Pong district. Officials emphasize rabies lethality and the importance of prevention. The initiative also extends to residents through mobile clinics providing general medical screenings, including blood pressure checks, diabetes, cancer screening, and HIV testing. Mobile health units will operate across Pattaya districts through the end of April.

article.articleHeadline: Anjing yang Diduga Terpapar Rabies Ngamuk Gigit 18 Warga di Bali
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dog suspected of having rabies goes on a rampage, bites 18 residents in Bali.
article.articleSummary: A dog suspected of rabies bit 18 residents in Banyuning Village, Buleleng District, Bali, Indonesia, on April 23, 2026; the animal remains at large as authorities conduct ongoing searches. All bite victims received anti-rabies vaccination and medical care, with none classified as high risk. Vaccination was provided at four health facilities, including Puskesmas Buleleng 3, Puskesmas Buleleng 1, and RSU Giri Emas. Among the victims, two were children aged 10 and 5. Most bites targeted the legs and hands. The incident was first detected via social media and subsequently confirmed by the Buleleng Health Office, which notes continued vigilance and outreach to prevent further attacks while containment efforts proceed.

triage.headline_ja: 狂犬病の疑いがある犬がバリ州で暴れて18人の住民に咬傷
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア（バリ州）での狂犬病疑い犬による咬傷事件で、複数の人的被害が発生しているがWPRO基準の異常性・重症度が部分的に該当。ただし全被害者がワクチン接種済みで高リスク者がいないため、WPROスクリーニング基準1つ以上の該当と社会的関心の兆候は認められるものの、現段階ではIHR基準2つ以上の明確な該当がないため、情報の続報を注視する段階と判定。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーから、バリ州ブレレン地区バニューニング村で2026年4月23日に発生した狂犬病疑い犬による咬傷事件。被害者18名（内小児2名）が確認されたが、全員がワクチン接種されており高リスク者がいない点が重要。犬はまだ逃げていることから長期曝露の可能性は検討の余地があるが、現段階ではWPRO基準の「異常性」のみが該当。社会的関心は存在し（ソーシャルメディア経由で検出、保健当局が対応）、引き続き情報収集が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Indea alerta produtores sobre foco de raiva bovina e convoca reunião em Alta Floresta " Notícia Exata - Notícias de Alta Floresta e Região!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Indea alerts producers about a bovine rabies outbreak and convenes a meeting in Alta Floresta
article.articleSummary: Indea Mato Grosso alerted cattle producers in Alta Floresta after confirming a bovine rabies focus in the Pista do Cabeça area. A meeting is scheduled for April 28 at 2:00 PM at Escola Estadual Boa Esperança to outline mandatory vaccination within a 10-km radius, due to circulation of hematophagous bats, the primary vectors. About 142 properties lie inside the danger zone, making producer participation essential for sanitary control. Technicians will explain obligatory vaccination of cattle and horses and discuss preventive measures and herd management. Vaccination is the main measure to prevent spread and protect livelihoods. As part of surveillance, a follow-up event will be held May 13 from 9:00 to 16:00 at the same venue, where producers must present vaccine invoices and an updated stock declaration. The outbreak is under control, but adherence to measures is critical; rabies is a viral disease affecting the nervous system of mammals and can affect humans.

triage.headline_ja: Indea（マット・グロッソ州農業開発局）がアルタ・フロレスタで牛狂犬病の発生を生産者に警告し会議を招集

triage.notes: 狂犬病は人獣共通感染症であり、記事では人間への影響の可能性を明示している。ハエトクコウモリ（hematophagous bats）が媒介として指摘されており、広範囲の生産者への強制予防接種が命令されている。現在は制御下にあると述べられているが、144件の農場が危険地域に位置しており、遵守率が重要である。追加の疫学的情報（死亡数、確認症例数など）が不足している。

article.articleHeadline: Researchers find new zombie ants in Brazilian jungle - Blast Magazine
article.articleSummary: Four new types of fungus have been identified in the Brazilian jungle that infect ants, hijack their bodies, and kill the hosts. David Hughes of Penn State identified the new species on a recent expedition to Brazil. The fungi infect ants when spores land on or are encountered on the forest floor or come from above; spores use enzymes to invade the body. About a week after infection, the ant wanders to vegetation and bites into leaves or nearby vegetation before dying; the fungus then grows from the ant’s head, enabling transmission to other ants. Researchers documented ant graveyards and noted many infected ants with mandibles attached to leaf veins, potentially aiding spread. The findings illustrate a diverse zombie-ant phenomenon in Brazil, with no details in the article about human infections or lab confirmation.

article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day: Risk in pregnancy explained with symptoms, complications and prevention tips
article.articleSummary: Malaria poses elevated risk during pregnancy in India, as highlighted on World Malaria Day 2026 (April 25). In New Delhi and other malaria-prone areas, pregnant women are more vulnerable to severe anaemia, high fever and weakness, with possible impacts on fetal growth, preterm delivery or pregnancy loss. Early detection is crucial; any fever during pregnancy should not be dismissed and warrants timely testing and safe treatment to reduce complications for mother and baby. Preventive measures remain essential: use insecticide-treated nets, wear protective clothing, maintain a clean home environment, and eliminate stagnant water to curb mosquito breeding. Regular antenatal care helps monitor health and detect infection early under medical supervision. With awareness, preventive care and prompt medical support, the risks of malaria in pregnancy can be effectively managed.

triage.headline_ja: 世界マラリアデー：妊娠中のリスクが症状、合併症、予防のヒントとともに説明される
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は世界マラリアデーの啓発キャンペーン記事であり、インド全体のマラリア流行に関する具体的な新規発生事例や異常な増加を報告していない。教育的・予防的な内容に焦点当てており、IHR基準やWPRO基準における懸念領域を満たさない。
triage.notes: 本記事は世界マラリアデー（4月25日）に関連した啓発記事であり、マラリアの既知のリスク要因や予防措置について一般的な情報を提供している。新規の流行、異常な症例増加、または管理能力の懸念を示す具体的な疫学データは含まれていない。ニューデリーおよびインドの他のマラリア流行地域での既知のリスクのみが言及されている。

article.articleHeadline: രോഗാണുക്കൾ കരളിലെത്തി രക്തകോശങ്ങളെ നശിപ്പിക്കും, മലേറിയക്കെതിരെയുള്ള പോരാട്ടത്തിൽ ജാഗ്രത പ്രധാനം
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pathogens reach the liver and destroy red blood cells; vigilance is paramount in the fight against malaria.
article.articleSummary: As of 25 April 2026, malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes. Infected individuals experience fever with chills, headache, body pains, vomiting, and marked weakness as parasites reach the liver and destroy red blood cells, causing anemia. Transmission occurs mainly via mosquito bites, but can also occur through blood transfusion and from mother to fetus during pregnancy. India aims to halt indigenous transmission by 2027 and become malaria-free by 2030, described as a nationwide grassroots movement combining vector control and timely treatment. Challenges include rising insecticide resistance and parasite resistance to antimalarials. Despite these hurdles, India reports more than an 80% drop in malaria cases and deaths over the past decade, earning removal from the WHO list of malaria-endemic countries. The author is a Community Medicine physician at Kochi Amrita Hospital.

triage.headline_ja: 病原体が肝臓に到達して赤血球を破壊する；マラリアとの闘いにおいて警戒が最重要

article.articleHeadline: OB dan Cleaning Service di RSUD Ratu Zalecha Banjar Diperkuat Cegah Penularan Penyakit Berbahaya - Banjarmasinpost.co.id
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Office Boy and Cleaning Service Staff at Ratu Zalecha Banjar Regional General Hospital Strengthened to Prevent the Transmission of Dangerous Diseases
article.articleSummary: At RSUD Ratu Zalecha in Martapura, Banjar Regional General Hospital, 75 Office Boy and cleaning service staff were trained as frontline guardians to prevent transmission of dangerous infections in the hospital. The Infection Prevention and Control (PPI) training, conducted in the hospital’s management hall, focused on protecting workers from exposure to blood and body fluids and addressing Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV. Training covered hand hygiene, proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE), cleaning techniques for patient areas, spill response for blood/body fluids, medical waste management, needle-stick injury prevention, cough etiquette, and occupational health. Participants also received instruction on protecting themselves in high-risk zones and ensuring Hepatitis B vaccination is mandatory. The program involved the PPI Team, IPCN, hospital PPI Committee, K3RS, and third-party PT Rasi Bintang Borneo, with on-site supervision to enforce SOPs. The hospital aims to increase SOP compliance and reduce healthcare-associated infections.

article.articleHeadline: World Malaria Day 2026: From fever to chills: Early warning signs you shouldn't ignore during malaria season
article.articleSummary: Malaria in India shows seasonal spikes, with delayed recognition a major concern. Early symptoms—fever with chills, headache, fatigue, and joint pain—can resemble flu or dengue. Malaria follows a cyclical pattern: fever rises, then falls and sweats, a key clue that should prompt testing. Nausea, stomach unease, or appetite loss may appear early, especially in children. If fever lasts more than 2–3 days with chills and fatigue, testing is advised; a rapid diagnostic test (RDT) can confirm infection quickly. Plasmodium falciparum can progress rapidly, and severe symptoms may develop within 24 hours if untreated, risking brain, kidneys, and lungs. Signs of complications include yellow eyes or dark urine. National guidance from the National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control emphasizes early diagnosis to prevent severe outcomes. Inputs from Dr Mandeep Singh (Fortis Hospital Ludhiana) and Dr Suchismitha Rajamanya (Aster Whitefield Hospital) reinforce awareness and timely action, alongside simple prevention measures.

article.articleHeadline: Pemprov Lampung Perkuat Layanan Kesehatan untuk Tekan TBC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lampung Provincial Government Strengthens Health Services to Curb TB.
article.articleSummary: Lampung Province, Indonesia, is intensifying Tuberculosis (TB) elimination through strengthened health services and digital data tools. Deputy Governor Jihan Nurlela told the Persatuan Dokter Paru Indonesia (PDPI) Lampung Branch on 24 April 2026 that Lampung, a national-priority area, will accelerate comprehensive TB elimination, drawing on COVID-19-era collaboration. The plan broadens early detection linked to treatment, and expands roles from Puskesmas and Posyandu to village health cadres, while piloting the Lampung In app for real-time patient monitoring. The Dinas Komunikasi, Informatika, dan Statistik will coordinate data bridging with PDPI. Health outcomes show progress: Standard Service Minimal indicators rose from 103% (2024) to 131% (2025); as of Q1 2026, SPM realization was 19%. TB cure rate with first-line drugs rose from 95% to 98% (2024–2025); Q1 2026 treatment achievement was 81%.

article.articleHeadline: Putri Koster Soroti Lonjakan Lalat di Kintamani Bali, Bisa Bawa Bakteri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Putri Koster Highlights a Fly Surge in Kintamani, Bali, That Can Carry Bacteria
article.articleSummary: Surge of houseflies in Kintamani, Bangli, Bali, raises concerns about bacterial transmission and broader public health. Bali's PKK chair Putri Koster urged environmental cleanliness and waste management during a socialization on Friday, April 24, 2026, in Desa Kintamani, Desa Pinggan, and Desa Sukawana. She emphasized source-separation of waste: organic waste compostable at households, markets, schools, and places of worship; inorganic waste sorted into recyclables managed at TPS3R and residuals handled by an incinerator. She highlighted community health awareness, citing a resident in Banjar Paketan, Sukawana with xerosis cutis who required medical care. Regarding animal health, she urged pet dog care and routine vaccination to prevent rabies; in case of dog bites, seek care at the nearest health facility promptly. The event underscores the strategic role of housewives in family health and environmental hygiene.

triage.headline_ja: プトリ・コスター、バリ州キンタマニのハエの急増に注目、細菌を運ぶ可能性がある

triage.notes: 記事の主題はハエの増加と環境衛生問題であり、狂犬病は予防策の文脈でのみ言及されている。実際の狂犬病患者の発症報告や流行の兆候は記載されていない。バリ州内の複数地域（キンタマニ、バングリなど）が関連地域として特定されているが、いずれもインドネシア国内。

article.articleHeadline: WHO urges immediate vaccination programme as measles risk high in Bangladesh
article.articleSummary: WHO urges immediate measles vaccination in Bangladesh to curb an ongoing outbreak, calling for 95% two-dose coverage across municipalities, strengthened surveillance, and rapid-response capacity. Emphasis is on high-traffic border areas, with trained rapid response teams and national protocols to contain imported cases and prevent re-establishment of endemic transmission. Close coordination between national and local authorities is essential. During outbreaks, hospitals should isolate patients and minimize in-hospital transmission. Vaccination priorities include healthcare workers, transport and tourism staff, international travelers, and migrant populations in border regions; ensure vaccine stockpiles and access for displaced and underserved groups. No travel or trade restrictions advised. National risk is high due to ongoing transmission, large susceptible child population, immunity gaps, and suspected deaths; about 91% of cases are 1–14 years old, with most unvaccinated or partially vaccinated. Cross-border movement with India and Myanmar heightens risk, especially in Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Cox's Bazar.

triage.headline_ja: WHOがバングラデシュの麻疹リスク高の中で予防接種プログラムの実施を促促す
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で3つ該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外な流行、国際的な拡大リスク）、WPRO基準で複数該当（異常性、重症度、流行易性、管理可能性への懸念）。バングラデシュにおける進行中の麻疹流行で、死亡疑い例、免疫ギャップのある大規模な易感染者人口、インド・ミャンマーとの越境移動によるリスク増大が確認され、フルRRAに進む必要がある。
triage.notes: バングラデシュが主たる発生国（Dhaka、Sylhet、Chattogram、Cox's Bazarで確認）。インド・ミャンマーとの越境移動によるリスクが明記されており、地域的に検証された3国すべてが関連。91%の症例が1-14歳で、大部分が未接種または部分接種。WHOが95%の二次投与カバレッジを呼びかけており、国際的な関心が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Penajam siapkan 2.650 dosis vaksin, antisipasi PMK jelang Idul Adha - ANTARA News Kalimantan Timur
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Penajam Prepares 2,650 Vaccine Doses, Anticipating Foot-and-Mouth Disease Ahead of Eid al-Adha - ANTARA News East Kalimantan
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (PMK) vaccination drive underway in Penajam Paser Utara Regency, East Kalimantan, Indonesia, ahead of Eid al-Adha 2026. The local government has prepared 2,650 vaccine doses to prevent PMK spread among cattle and goats; vaccination has begun. The district houses about 8,500 cattle and around 387 goats, with most animals already vaccinated; vaccination data are recorded in the National Animal Health Information System with owner identification. In the lead-up to Eid, intensive herd checks will be conducted at farms and at animal market sites to ensure only healthy stock is sacrificed. A stringent quarantine protocol mandates 100% health checks for livestock entering the district from outside, and vigilance over cross-regional animal movements. Traders typically bring livestock from outside about a month before Eid; entrants must be free of PMK and Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD).

triage.headline_ja: ペナジャム、イード・アル＝アドハーに向け口蹄疫対策として2,650用量のワクチンを準備 - アンタラ・ニュース東カリマンタン
triage.triage_reason: 動物由来感染症（口蹄疫およびルンピー皮膚病）の予防的ワクチン接種活動であり、現在のところ発生報告ではなく「予防対策」段階。IHR基準は2つ以上該当しないため PICKUPには至らず、ただし家畜疫病の監視対象として経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 記事は既知の家畜疫病（口蹄疫・ルンピー皮膚病）に対する予防的ワクチン接種プログラムの報告であり、現在のところ発病事例の報告ではない。イード・アル＝アドハーに向けた家畜市場での疾病リスク管理の観点から、疫学的な監視継続に値するが、即座のフルRRA対象とはならない。インドネシア国内での対応能力は確保されている。

article.articleHeadline: विश्व मलेरिया दिवस आज,  तीन वर्ष में छह गुना बढ़ गए मलेरिया के मरीज, बचाव और समय पर इलाज पर जोर
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Malaria Day Today: Malaria Cases Have Risen Sixfold in Three Years, with Emphasis on Prevention and Timely Treatment.
article.articleSummary: On 25 April 2026 (World Malaria Day) in Lucknow, India, malaria burden is rising, with cases increasing from 97 in 2023 to about 676 in 2025 (roughly six- to seven-fold). Despite awareness campaigns, fogging and anti-larva spraying are claimed ongoing control measures. Chief Medical Officer Dr NB Singh attributes better awareness to timely hospital visits, while District Malaria Officer Ritu Srivastav notes continued fogging and larvicide application and emphasizes identifying symptomatic patients for testing. Malaria is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes; prevention hinges on protection from mosquitoes and prompt treatment to prevent fatalities. Common symptoms include fever, headache, and chills, typically appearing 10–15 days post-infection, with severe signs such as extreme fatigue, fainting, breathing difficulties, blood in urine, jaundice (yellow eyes/skin), and abnormal bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: ワールドマラリアデー2026年：3年間でマラリア患者が6倍に増加、予防と適切な治療に重点
triage.triage_reason: インド・ウッタルプラデーシュ州ラクノウでのマラリア患者数が3年間で約676例まで急増（2023年の97例から約6-7倍）しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と予防措置の効果不足が懸念される。国内での著しい増加傾向と媒介蚊対策の継続的な需要が確認されている。
triage.notes: 2026年4月25日はワールドマラリアデー。記事はルクノウ（ウッタルプラデーシュ州）での疾患負荷増加を報告。患者数の6-7倍増加は異常で、媒介蚊対策（fogging、幼虫駆除薬散布）が継続中であるが効果が限定的。地域レベルでの爆発的増加が確認されており、WPROスクリーニング基準5項目すべてに該当。IHR基準は「深刻な公衆衛生影響」と「異常性」で2項目該当。

article.articleHeadline: La OMS precalifica 'Coartem Baby' (Novartis) para el tratamiento de la malaria en recién nacidos y lactantes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO prequalifies 'Coartem Baby' (Novartis) for the treatment of malaria in newborns and infants.
article.articleSummary: WHO prequalifies Coartem Baby (artemether-lumefantrine) for malaria treatment in newborns and infants weighing 2–5 kg, the first and only antimalarial designed specifically for the smallest patients. The WHO prequalification evaluates quality, safety, and efficacy and informs UN agencies and other buyers’ financing and public-sector procurement decisions to expand access in malaria-endemic regions. Until recently there was no approved product for neonates under 4.5 kg, forcing use of formulations intended for older children and increasing toxicity risk. In Ankaase Methodist Hospital, Ghana, clinicians have faced uncertainty when treating very young infants; Coartem Baby offers age-appropriate dosing. Developed by Novartis with scientific and financial support from Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) as part of the PAMAfrica consortium, and co-financed by EDCTP and SIDA. MMV CEO Martin Fitchet calls the prequalification a public-health milestone; Novartis highlights improved access for the smallest babies.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、新生児および乳幼児のマラリア治療用『コアルテム ベビー』（ノバルティス）を事前認定
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は医薬品の規制認定（WHO事前認定）に関するニュースであり、新規の感染症発生イベントではない。ガーナの新規マラリア流行、患者増加、異常な疫学的事象を報告するものではなく、既存疾患対策の医療ツール改善についての公式な治療薬認定である。
triage.notes: 記事はガーナで発生中の新規マラリア流行やアウトブレイクについて報告するものではなく、WHOが医薬品（コアルテム ベビー）をマラリア治療用として事前認定したことを伝える規制ニュースである。既知の風土病対策における医療介入の進展を扱うもので、シグナル検出（突発的な感染症イベント）の対象外。

article.articleHeadline: Haryana's Novel Efforts Propel Malaria Elimination Drive | Health
article.articleSummary: Malaria elimination efforts in Haryana, India, are advancing through micro-surveillance, source tracing, and high-risk population monitoring at village and mohalla levels to ensure early detection and rapid treatment. The Health Department has conducted over 950 door-to-door surveys this month and instituted mandatory investigations for every reported malaria case, with epidemiologists forming specialized teams to trace infection sources and address transmission. The program introduces monthly labour-site inspections and rapid diagnostic tests to accelerate confirmation and response. The initiatives align with the global campaign 'Driven to End Malaria: Now We Can. Now We Must' and have yielded a steady decline in malaria cases, reflecting Haryana’s commitment to a malaria-free future. The approach emphasizes timely detection, case investigation, and targeted interventions to interrupt transmission in high-risk areas.

triage.headline_ja: ハリヤナ州のマラリア撲滅活動が新たな取り組みで前進
triage.triage_reason: マラリア撲滅に向けた正常な公衆衛生活動の進展報告。異常な流行や危機的状況ではなく、むしろ症例減少傾向を示しており、シグナルとしての特性を欠く。
triage.notes: 記事は感染症の流行ではなく、マラリア撲滅に向けた正常な公衆衛生プログラムの成功例を報告している。症例の減少傾向が明示されており、危機管理のトリアージ対象外。

article.articleHeadline: Hiểu lầm thường gặp về bệnh dại khi bị chó mèo cắn
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Common misconceptions about rabies when bitten by dogs or cats.
article.articleSummary: Rabies in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: 3 deaths this year, vs 5 in all of last year, amid warnings the disease could spike in hot weather. The virus is shed in animal saliva and can transmit via bites, scratches, licking open wounds, or contact with mucous membranes, so even minor injuries from dogs or cats can cause infection. Post-exposure prophylaxis is an emergency: immediately wash the wound with soap under running water for at least 15 minutes, disinfect, and seek medical care; control heavy bleeding with clean gauze and proceed to a clinic promptly. Vaccine regimens depend on prior vaccination, exposure, wound severity, and animal status—unvaccinated individuals typically receive 5 intramuscular doses (days 0,3,7,14,28) or 8 intradermal doses (days 0,3,7,28) with adjustments after 10 days. Pre-exposure vaccination is advised for high-risk groups. Summer heat may increase dog/cat aggression; owners should vaccinate pets and keep them contained, while people, especially children, should avoid approaching stray animals.

triage.headline_ja: 犬や猫に咬まれた際の狂犬病に関する一般的な誤解
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム（ホーチミン市）での狂犬病による3例の死亡報告があり、季節的な流行リスク警告もあるが、情報が主に公衆衛生啓発・予防指導の性質であり、現在の流行状況の詳細が不明。
triage.notes: 記事の主な内容は狂犬病の啓発・予防指導であり、現在の流行規模の詳細情報（患者数、検査陽性数など）が不足している。ホーチミン市での2026年の3例死亡（前年同期5例）は重症度を示す一方、これが異常値かどうかは判断困難。季節的な流行増加の警告が示されており、スクリーニング基準では複数該当。情報が増えれば PICKUP への昇格可能性あり。

article.articleHeadline: Haryana intensifies fight against malaria with targeted micro plans, community outreach
article.articleSummary: On World Malaria Day, Haryana intensified malaria elimination with village- and mohalla-level micro-surveillance, source tracing, and high-risk population monitoring. The plan covers all areas that reported malaria last year, plus routine health-worker activities. Health teams have conducted over 950 door-to-door surveys to ensure early detection. Every reported case now undergoes mandatory investigation by a specialized epidemiology team to identify the infection source and contain spread at the origin. A monthly labour-site inspection program targets vulnerable groups to reduce transmission. The initiatives align with the theme Driven to End Malaria: Now We Can. Now We Must. Haryana’s malaria burden has fallen from 4,485 cases in 2014 to 2025’s 202, with no malaria deaths. Of 2025’s 515 cases, 202 were within the state; the remainder linked to other states. Eight cases were reported as of March 31, 2026. Field surveys will rely on rapid diagnostic tests; microscopy remains the institute-level mainstay.

triage.headline_ja: ハリヤナ州、対象的なマイクロプラン及びコミュニティアウトリーチによるマラリア対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: マラリア患者数は大幅に減少（2014年4,485件→2026年8件）し、死亡ゼロ。公衆衛生上の深刻な影響は認められず、既存の疾病管理活動の強化報道である。
triage.notes: ハリヤナ州はインド内の1州であり、発生地域リストにも含まれている。記事はワールドマラリアデーの文脈での予防・啓発活動に焦点を当てており、新規の感染症危機ではなく、既存疾病の継続的な管理強化を報道している。マラリア患者数の継続的な減少傾向が確認されており、シグナルとして識別する根拠は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: VIT Bhopal Admissions के बीच बवाल, स्टूडेंट्स में टाइफाइड का सामूहिक संक्रमण, दूषित पेयजल का मामला
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Row over VIT Bhopal admissions, typhoid outbreak among students, case of contaminated drinking water.
article.articleSummary: Typhoid fever outbreak at VIT Bhopal (Sehore district, near Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) affects over 250 hostel residents, with 13 new typhoid positives in the last 24 hours. The campus lies about 80 km from Bhopal city, in a village in Sehore, far from city healthcare and drinking-water sources. Chirayu Medical College pathology reports corroborate typhoid cases; Dr. Ajay Goyanka stated that some students tested positive. University management has dismissed reports as rumors, claiming only 80 students had a seasonal viral illness, while parents have messaged Bhopal media and medicines for typhoid have been purchased locally. As a precaution, the administration sent home the 2025 batch. SDOP Damodar Gupta warned the university to bring the situation under control or face responsibility if violence recurs, as in November 2025. Health experts blame contaminated drinking water or hostel-food handling and water-tank sanitation for this mass infection.

triage.headline_ja: VIT Bhopal入学をめぐる騒動、学生の集団チフス感染、汚染水道水の問題
triage.triage_reason: インドのVIT Bhopal校内で250人以上が影響を受けるチフス集団感染が発生。直近24時間で13人の新規確定患者を含む異常事態であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響とWPRO基準の複数項目が該当する。
triage.notes: VIT Bhopalはセホーレ地区（Bhopal近郊）の村にある大学で、都市部の医療施設から80km離れている。汚染水道水が原因と指摘されており、長期的な曝露リスク（水タンク衛生問題）が継続している。大学管理部と学生・保護者の間に情報のズレがあり、政治的問題化の可能性も指摘されている（2025年11月の暴力事件の前例）。

article.articleHeadline: রাজধানীতে ম্যালেরিয়া নিয়ে দুঃসংবাদ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bad news about malaria in the capital.
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a threat in Bangladesh, with Dhaka—the capital—now facing locally detected vectors. In the first quarter of 2026, 460 malaria cases were reported nationwide; last year’s cases exceeded 10,100 with 16 deaths. Surveillance in Dhaka North City (3–7 April) found Anopheles vectors in six zones; Jahangirnagar University reported 98 Anopheles in a single week, and by 15 April more than 2,500 were recorded in those zones. Experts warn that once transmission establishes in Dhaka, control becomes difficult. Severe malaria can damage organs and the brain; fatalities can be rapid. Antimalarial drugs are scarce in the open market; authorities supply treatment, while stockpiling and vaccines are urged. Commerce Secretary Mabubur Rahman died of malaria on 17 April; infection source remains unclear, with Cameroon travel noted. Imported cases from Myanmar and India and sporadic local transmission are considerations for containment.

triage.headline_ja: 首都でのマラリアに関する悪いニュース
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の都市部での局所伝播、国際的拡大リスク）。WPROスクリーニング基準複数該当。高い政治的関心（大臣死亡）と国際的支援ニーズあり。
triage.notes: バングラデシュ（対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations に含めない）での主要イベントですが、記事は輸入症例源としてインドとミャンマーを明示。政治的に高い注目度：バングラデシュの商務大臣がマラリアで死亡。蚊媒介対策（ベクター検出）と医薬品不足が重要な公衆衛生課題として言及されている。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria deaths drop sharply; infections remain high- GHS  - MyJoyOnline
article.articleSummary: Malaria deaths in Ghana fell from about 3,300 in 2011 to 52 in 2025, a >98% reduction per the Ghana Health Service’s National Malaria Elimination Programme. Inpatient malaria mortality declined from 0.21 per 1,000 in 2024 to 0.15 in 2025, linked to improved diagnosis and treatment. Yet infections remain high: 2024 recorded ~4.3 million confirmed cases from over 12 million suspected. Facility testing reached ~99%, but fewer than half of suspected cases were confirmed, indicating fever misclassification. Malaria risk dropped from 28% in 2011 to ~8.6% now; Greater Accra (~2%) has the lowest transmission. Vulnerable groups include children under five and pregnant women (89% had at least one IPT dose; completion was low). ITN distribution reached ~87% of target and 85% for ongoing distribution; funding limits expansion of IRS and preventive programs. Ghana targets 90% mortality reduction and 50% incidence cut by 2028, with 21 districts identified for elimination. World Malaria Day 2026 theme: Driven to End Malaria: Now We Can. Now We Must.

triage.headline_ja: マラリア死亡数が急減、感染数は依然高い - ガーナ保健局
triage.triage_reason: マラリア死亡の大幅改善は好ましい傾向だが、依然高い感染数と予防プログラムの資金制約から、持続的な対策課題が存在。情報は確定的だがリスク見通しの確認が必要。
triage.notes: マラリアは風土病として長期にわたり国民に曝露し、脆弱層（5歳未満小児、妊婦）への影響が継続。2028年の目標達成に向けた資金制約が管理可能性の課題。IHR基準には該当しないため PICKUP ではなく、スクリーニング基準複数該当と政府関心から WATCH 判定。

article.articleHeadline: Jamin Kesehatan Warga Binaan, Rutan Salatiga Tangani Kasus DBD dengan Prosedur Medis Ketat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Guaranteeing Inmates' Health, Salatiga Detention Center Handles Dengue Fever Cases with Strict Medical Procedures.
article.articleSummary: Salatiga Detention Center in Indonesia referred a prisoner to Dr. Asmir DKT Hospital for intensive care on Saturday, 25 April 2026, after dengue fever and typhoid fever were diagnosed. The inmate developed high fever, headache, and weakness; despite initial in-house treatment, condition deteriorated, prompting a strict escorted transfer by security staff, the jail physician, and police. Hospital tests confirmed co-infection with dengue fever and typhoid fever, requiring continued intensive care. Rutan Salatiga’s Acting Head, Ruwiyanto, said the referral reflects the center’s commitment to optimal inmate health, with in-house polyclinic care and medical staff, and escalation to external hospitals according to procedures. The Detention Center will maintain heightened monitoring and health services to safeguard inmates’ basic rights as long as treatment is needed.

triage.headline_ja: 収容者の健康を保証、サラティガ拘置所は厳格な医療手順でデング熱症例に対応
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア（対象国）の拘置所でデング熱と腸チフスの併発患者が確認されたが、発生規模が限定的（単一患者）で、現時点では国際的な拡大リスクが明確ではない。情報が限定的なため、経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 記事は拘置所内での単一患者の入院ケースを報告しており、集団発生の兆候は報告されていない。デング熱と腸チフスは共に蚊媒介および人口密集地で流行しやすい疾患であり、拘置所は高リスク環境である。ただし、発生規模や死亡の報告はなく、現段階ではWATCHレベルの評価が適切。続報で集団発生の確認があればPICKUPへ昇格される可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: ಮಲೇರಿಯಾ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಮುಂಜಾಗ್ರತೆ ವಹಿಸುವುದು ಅಗತ್ಯ - Sanjevani
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: It is essential to exercise caution regarding malaria.
article.articleSummary: On 25 April 2026, Kalaburagi observed World Malaria Day at Shahabjhar Nagar Primary Health Centre, in collaboration with the Basaveshwar Social Service Group. Dr. Anupama Keshwar warned that malaria’s key symptoms include chills, fever, and nausea, and urged prompt diagnostic testing and appropriate treatment. She emphasized not fearing malaria while adopting preventive measures. Malaria is transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes that breed in standing water, so households should prevent water stagnation, maintain cleanliness, secure water storage, and use mosquito nets and repellents. Additional guidance included drinking boiled or treated water, maintaining a balanced diet, and minimizing exposure during rainfall. The event was led by HB Patil (president and lecturer) with participation from social workers and health-centre staff, including Shivayogappa S. Biradar, to promote prevention and early care.

triage.headline_ja: マラリアについて慎重になることが必要である
triage.triage_reason: この記事はインドのカルナータカ州カラブルギで開催されたWorld Malaria Dayに関するイベント報道であり、既知の風土病について注意喚起するコンテンツです。新たな流行や異常な症例の増加を示す公衆衛生シグナルではありません。
triage.notes: 記事はインドのマラリア風土病地域における予防キャンペーンに関する報道であり、特定の事例や異常な流行の兆候は記載されていません。World Malaria Day開催という定期的なイベント報道にすぎません。

article.articleHeadline: Rätselhafte Krankheit in Burundi: Fünf Tote und 35 Infizierte - WHO ermittelt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mysterious Disease in Burundi: Five Dead and 35 Infected — WHO Investigating.
article.articleSummary: Five dead and 35 infected in northern Burundi from an as-yet unknown disease; WHO and local authorities are jointly investigating, with an expert field team on site to support investigations and care. Alarm was raised in late March after several cases emerged within the same family and environment. Affected individuals show fever, vomiting, diarrhea, blood in urine, fatigue, and abdominal pain; severe cases involve jaundice and anemia. Early laboratory analyses have been partially reassuring, as tests for Ebola, Marburg, yellow fever, and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever were negative, but the cause remains unclear. Health Minister Lydwine Badarahana emphasized ongoing investigations and protective measures to prevent spread. The WHO assists with surveillance, field investigations, clinical care, laboratory diagnostics, infection prevention and control, and logistics. Additional tests are underway, with samples sent to the Democratic Republic of Congo for further analysis to identify the source.

triage.headline_ja: ブルンジの謎の病気：5人死亡、35人感染 — WHOが調査中
triage.triage_reason: 未知の出血熱様疾患で死亡・重症化があり、複数のIHR基準と全てのWPRO基準を満たす。WHOが現地調査チームを派遣し、国際的な公衆衛生対応が進行中。
triage.notes: Bluedotが付与した発生地域にはBurundi（433561）が含まれているが、記事サマリーの主題はブルンジの疾患発生であり、DRCは検査送付先として言及されているのみ。ただし、DRCも対象国リストに含まれ、ウイルス同定のため当該国への検査送付が既に進行中であるため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを含めた。ブルンジ（対象国外）での発生が主体であることに留意。マルブルグ、エボラ、黄熱、CCHFの初期検査が陰性だが原因不明という状況、並びにWHOが現地調査チーム派遣・国際的監視体制の構築により、シグナルとしての重要性は極めて高い。

article.articleHeadline: Paso de gigante de la ciencia: los drones con IA ya detectan criaderos de mosquitos transmisores de enfermedades
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A giant leap for science: AI-powered drones are already detecting breeding grounds of disease-spreading mosquitoes.
article.articleSummary: Stanford researchers deploy AI-powered drones to locate Aedes aegypti breeding grounds in Makassar, Indonesia, focusing on the Tallo district over about four square kilometers. Drones with high-resolution cameras capture imagery that two CNNs, U-Net++ and DeepLabV3++, analyze to identify discarded tires with standing water—the principal larval habitats. The models achieved F1 scores of 0.87 and 0.82, respectively, and detected nearly twice as many breeding sites as ground inspection teams, including objects partially hidden by shadows or vegetation. The system promises lower operational costs and rapid, district-wide surveillance that far exceeds traditional ground patrols. Aedes aegypti transmits dengue, Zika, and chikungunya; dengue remains the most widespread, with Zika having triggered a 2016 international emergency. Planned improvements include detecting other water-holding waste, incorporating multispectral imagery, adapting models to different geographies, and integrating AI-enabled drones into urban surveillance protocols for proactive outbreak prevention.

triage.headline_ja: 科学の大躍進：AI搭載ドローンが病気媒介蚊の繁殖地を検出
triage.triage_reason: AI技術を用いた蚊の繁殖地検出に関する研究報告であり、直接的な感染症の新規発生や急速な拡大を示すイベントではない。ただし、対象地域（インドネシア）でのデング熱・ジカ・チクングニアの媒介蚊対策の進展は公衆衛生上の関心があり、今後の実装状況を注視する価値がある。
triage.notes: 本記事は感染症イベント（患者発生・流行）ではなく、公開研究・技術展開に関する報道である。Bluedot APIが疾患名（Zika、Chikungunya、Dengue）を抽出したのは、記事に媒介蚊と疾患の関連性が記載されているためと推定される。実際の疾患の新規流行を示すシグナルではないため、PICKUP対象外。ただし、媒介蚊対策技術の有効性が確認され、インドネシアでの実装が進行する場合、将来的な疫学対策への影響は注視する価値がある。

article.articleHeadline: Sud-Kivu : plus de 10.000 cas de rougeole dont 72 décès enregistrés depuis janvier 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: South Kivu: more than 10,000 measles cases, of which 72 deaths have been recorded since January 2026.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, with 10,065 cases and 72 deaths since January 2026 as of April 24, 2026. The majority of fatalities occurred in hard-to-reach health zones: Shabunda (18 deaths), Kamituga (12), and Kalole and Mulungu. According to Justin Bengehya, the provincial health surveillance chief, nearly all health zones in South Kivu are experiencing an outbreak, with exceptions in Minembwe and the upland areas of Uvira. Response measures include free treatment and targeted vaccination campaigns. The province is also contending with a cholera outbreak and additional monkeypox (variole du singe) cases. Authorities warn of rising measles cases across the province; vaccination and rapid response are underway to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 南キブ州：2026年1月以降、麻疹患者10,000人以上、死亡者72人を記録
triage.triage_reason: 麻疹の大規模流行（10,065例、72死亡）がDRC南キブ州で進行中であり、IHR基準3項目（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）に該当。WPROスクリーニング基準でも4項目（異常性、重症度、長期曝露、流行しやすさ）に該当。コレラとモンキーポックスの同時流行も報告されており、早期の詳細アセスメント（フルRRA）が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCの南キブ州における麻疹流行を主題としており、死亡率は約0.7%（72/10,065）。複数の困難地域（Shabunda、Kamituga、Kalole、Mulungu）で重症化と死亡が集中している。同時にコレラとモンキーポックスも流行中とのことで、複合的な感染症危機の状況。ブラジル（パライーバ州）はBluedot APIで地域として抽出されているが、記事サマリーに記載がないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: 腸病毒71型為何危險 7年未流行後重症風險升高-大纪元健康
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Why Is Enterovirus 71 Dangerous? After Seven Years Without an Outbreak, the Risk of Severe Illness Increases - Epoch Times Health
article.articleSummary: Enterovirus 71 (EV71) is highly neurotropic with rapid progression; severe infections can cause encephalitis and cardiopulmonary failure, with up to 20% mortality and potential long-term neurological sequelae. In Taiwan, EV71 accounts for most severe enterovirus cases since 2005, but no large outbreak since 2019—over seven years. Owing to COVID-19 measures and reduced natural exposure, immunity debt may raise severe risk if EV71 is reintroduced from Southeast Asia, where activity is rising (Vietnam). About 53% of adult EV infections are asymptomatic, and household transmission can reach 50–60%. Current surveillance shows no EV71-dominant circulation; Coxsackie A6 and A16 predominate. High-risk groups: children under 6, especially under 2. Red flags: persistent drowsiness, repeated vomiting, seizures, rapid breathing, tachycardia. Prevention relies on vaccination: privately available EV71 vaccines with ~99% efficacy and ≥5-year antibody duration; start at 2 months, three doses before age 2, or two doses after age 2.

triage.headline_ja: 腸病毒71型為何危險 7年未流行後重症風險升高
triage.triage_reason: エンテロウイルス71型は神経親和性が高く重症化リスクが高いが、記事は主に教育的・啓発的内容であり、現在の大規模流行は報告されていない。ただし東南アジア（ベトナム）での活動増加とワクチン未接種者の免疫低下による潜在的リスクのため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 台湾は対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations から除外。記事はEV71の重症化リスクと流行可能性に関する啓発記事であり、現在の確定した大規模流行報告ではなく、また台湾については「2019年以降の大規模流行なし」と記載されている。ベトナムでの活動増加が地域的脅威となる可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Kemenkes tekankan batas waktu 4 jam cegah cemaran bakteri dapur gizi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health emphasizes a four-hour deadline to prevent bacterial contamination in the nutrition kitchen.
article.articleSummary: As of 25 April 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia, the Ministry of Health emphasizes a four-hour maximum from cooking through portioning to distribution to prevent bacterial growth and foodborne poisoning in the national nutrition program (SPPG). Dr. Then Suyanti notes contamination risk begins at storage and travels to the consumer, so kitchens and SPPG must ensure even cooking, especially for large portions, and that distribution vehicles are clean and dedicated to food to avoid cross-contamination. E. coli has been repeatedly found in water used in cooking; despite National Nutrition Board water-treatment guidance, outputs should be tested regularly. Two-layer surveillance applies: internal by kitchen managers and external by Puskesmas, which perform Environmental Health Inspections and sampling with sanitarian tools. The Fast Response Team will investigate suspected outbreaks, and laboratory findings will inform improvements in SPPG food safety management to achieve zero food accidents.

triage.headline_ja: 保健省が栄養給食調理室での細菌汚染防止のため4時間の期限を強調
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアの栄養給食プログラムにおけるE. coli汚染リスクの管理強化に関する公式発表であり、異常/予想外の感染症イベントではなく、予防的ガイダンスの再強調。現在のところ患者発生の報告なし。
triage.notes: 本記事は感染症アウトブレイク報告ではなく、インドネシア保健省による栄養給食プログラムにおける食品安全管理の予防的ガイダンス再強調である。E. coliが過去に水から検出された履歴があるが、現在のところ患者発生報告なし。フルRRA不要だが、今後のE. coli関連アウトブレイク報告があれば迅速に対応する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Hallan bacterias de tuberculosis humana en entornos de gorilas en libertad del Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Human tuberculosis bacteria found in the habitats of wild gorillas in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: An international team including the Complutense University of Madrid (UCM) detected environmental DNA of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in wild gorilla habitats in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, marking the first TB DNA detection in free-ranging gorillas. Analyzing 178 environmental samples from hospitals, local communities, primate rehabilitation centers, and national parks, TB DNA was found in more than one-third of samples. Genomic patterns shared between human and gorilla TB strains suggest interspecies transmission, underscoring the need for integrated control strategies within a One Health framework. The study, published in Emerging Microbes & Infections, used sponge-based environmental sampling (eDNA) to non-invasively detect pathogen material on surfaces and in feces without direct animal handling. Collaborators include the Institute for Research in Game Resources (IREC) at the University of Castilla-La Mancha, the National Microbiology Center, French clinical microbiology labs, and Congolese Cinquantenaire de Lwiro and Kinshasa facilities. Implications for conservation of critically endangered gorillas and broader public health surveillance are highlighted.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴの野生ゴリラの生息地で人間の結核菌が発見される
triage.triage_reason: 結核のヒト-動物間感染疑い（One Health関連）および新規検出であり異常性がある。ただし、現時点では人間への直接的な健康被害や国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限の可能性が不明である。引き続き情報収集が必要。
triage.notes: スペインの大学が研究に参画しているが、実際の結核イベント発生地はコンゴである。ヒト-動物間の病原体伝播という One Health の文脈で重要だが、現段階ではゴリラ個体群への影響が主であり、人間への伝播リスクや広域的な公衆衛生上の脅威について詳細な情報が不足。eDNA検出であり、生きた菌による感染の証拠ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Afrika'da sıtmayla mücadelede tehdit devam ediyor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The threat to the fight against malaria in Africa continues.
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a persistent threat in Sub-Saharan Africa despite progress over the past decade. The region bears the majority of global cases, with Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, Ethiopia, and Mozambique driving the burden. In Cameroon, about 3 million malaria cases were reported in 2023, with deaths predominantly among children aged 6–59 months. Vector control—especially insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS)—is central to prevention, but misuse, rapid net wear, and insecticide resistance undermine impact. Rapid diagnostic tests, effective treatments, and malaria vaccines show promise: RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M reduce child mortality, and Cameroon added malaria vaccination to its routine schedule in January 2024. Climate changes—higher temperatures and irregular rainfall—expand mosquito habitats, while resistance in mosquitoes and parasites challenges control. Strengthened health systems, sustained funding, and international cooperation are essential to reach zero malaria.
